newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up across the board on Monday boosted by the strong performance of the domestic A share markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 12.48 percent from 8.38 percent on Wednesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market surged to 19.9 million lots from 5.2 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
The domestic A share markets surged 3.90 percent to end at 1,513.303 points on Monday, which fanned fund demand on the repurchase market, traders said.
"Institutions including securities houses were the most active traders who borrowed heavily to trade on the A share markets," said one trader.
Trading was very active with total volume hitting a new year-high due to the bullish stock markets, traders said.
"One new issue of 75 million shares today was another positive factor boosting trading volume," another trader said.
Traders said they believed the rates would undergo a minor correction in the next few days but would still remain at high levels.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended down on Monday on an expected correction after several days' gains before the holiday, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell to 120.20 yuan from 120.70 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market fell to 790,322 lots from 1.1 million lots.
